query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Co-doping the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a small amount of Yttrium (Y) and Hafnium (Hf) will improve its high-temperature stability, reduce oxide spallation under corrosive conditions, and enhance its resistance to long-term creep and cycling loads relevant to aerospace fasteners.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar microstructure consisting of FCC and BCC/B2 phases that shows limited resistance to grain growth, creep, and corrosion under extreme conditions.
generation.intervention: Introduce minor concentrations of Y and Hf (co-doping) into the alloy composition during processing (e.g., via laser cladding) to form a modified alloy (YHf-EHEA).
generation.conditions: Exposure to extreme temperature fluctuations (e.g., heat treatment at around 900 °C), corrosive environments (e.g., molten salts such as 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl) and long-term mechanical loading that simulate operational conditions for aircraft/spacecraft fasteners.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of an Al-rich L12 precipitate within the FCC phase and reduced grain growth, leading to a more thermally stable microstructure with improved oxide adhesion.
generation.mechanism: Y and Hf doping is expected to slow grain boundary mobility, stabilize precipitate formation, and enhance the adhesion of the protective oxide scale. This reduces grain coarsening and spallation of the oxide layer, thereby mitigating mechanisms that lead to creep and corrosion under high temperatures and cyclic loads.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the undoped alloy, the YHf co-doped EHEA will exhibit lower grain growth, reduced oxide spallation, enhanced resistance to high-temperature corrosion and improved creep behavior, resulting in a better strength–ductility balance under practical conditions.
generation.baseline: The performance of the as-deposited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy, which shows higher grain growth and greater oxide spallation under similar heat treatment and corrosive conditions.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to the lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloy processed via techniques such as laser cladding and subjected to high-temperature corrosive environments. Its applicability to other processing routes or compositions beyond the studied range is uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: It remains unclear how the co-doping with Y and Hf will affect long-term room-temperature creep under mechanical loading and whether any unforeseen phase or microstructural changes might emerge over extended operational cycles.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of coatings using laser cladding: one set with the baseline AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA composition, and another set with added Y and Hf (YHf-EHEA). Subject both sets to heat treatments at 900 °C for 10 hours and then expose them to a corrosive environment consisting of molten salts (75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl) at the same temperature. Additionally, perform long-term creep tests at room temperature under constant mechanical loading to simulate service conditions.
measurements: Quantitative analysis of grain size evolution using microscopy (SEM/TEM) before and after heat treatment.
Measurement of the percentage area affected by oxide scale spallation after hot corrosion exposure.
Creep lifetime and strain rate measurements under controlled mechanical loading.
Phase and precipitate analysis by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron diffraction techniques to identify the formation of the Al-rich L12 phase.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the YHf co-doped samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in grain growth, oxide scale spallation, and improved creep life compared to the baseline, or if they exhibit detrimental microstructural changes that compromise the strength–ductility balance, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractBoth crack-free AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) and Y and Hf co-doping AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA (YHf-EHEA) coatings were prepared by laser cladding. The solidification microstructure, thermal stability, and hot corrosion performance of the coatings at 900 °C under 75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl molten salts were investigated. The experimental results showed that the structure of the as-deposited coatings consisted of FCC and BCC/B2 phases. After heat treatment, an Al-rich L12 phase was precipitated in the FCC phase of all coatings. The grain sizes of the EHEA and YHf-EHEA coatings after heat treatment at 900 °C for 10 h increased by 27.5% and 15.7%, respectively, compared to the as-deposited coatings. Meanwhile, after hot corrosion, the spallation areas of the YHf-EHEA and EHEA coatings accounted for 14.98% and 5.67% of the total surface area, respectively. In this study, the Y and Hf co-doping did not change the microstructure morphology and phase structure of the coatings but did improve the thermal stability and resistance of the hot corrosion oxide scale spallation, providing a certain amount of data and theoretical support for the application of EHEA coat

## Abstract
Recent studies indicate that eutectic high-entropy alloys can simultaneously possess high strength and high ductility, which have potential industrial applications. The present study focuses on Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a lamellar dual-phase (fcc + B2) precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy. This alloy exhibits an fcc + B2 (B2 with bcc nano-precipitates) microstructure resulting in a combination of the soft and ductile fcc phase together with hard B2 phase. Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength. The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism. The alloy was tested under quasi-static (strain-rate = 10−3 s−1) tensile loading and dynamic (strain-rate = 103 s−1) compressive loading. Due to the fine lamellar microstructure with a large number of fcc-bcc interfaces, the alloy show relatively high flow-stresses, ~1400 MPa under quasi-static loading and in excess of 1800 MPa under dynamic loading.
